analysis.session_summary: The full-day tape was dominated by the 14:30 US employment report: payrolls printed 29K vs a 89K forecast, a normal miss that sent the dollar weaker by 0.097%. The NFP impulse was the only clearly causal move in many pairs; EUR/USD jumped 57.6 pips on that leg, while most earlier legs were catalyst-free. FX ranking showed AUD as strongest (+0.331%) and CAD weakest (-0.277%), with JPY also weak despite a Tokyo CPI beat. VIX closed down 3.027%, and EUR/USD finished the day at 1.12563, up 37.7 pips.

themes.theme: Dollar selloff concentrated in NFP reaction
themes.evidence: USD strength -0.216%; NFP actual 29K vs forecast 89K, own impulse -0.097%; Gold/USD +0.866%, USD/JPY -0.292%
AUD strength +0.331%, GBP +0.141%, EUR +0.121%; AUD/USD +37.8 pips, GBP/USD +47.1 pips

themes.theme: JPY and CAD lag with contrasting reasons
themes.evidence: JPY strength -0.238% despite Tokyo CPI beat at 2.7% vs 2.4%; CAD -0.277% with no own release and attempt rejected

currency_drivers.USD: NFP miss (29K vs 89K) drove USD weaker 0.097% in its own reaction.
currency_drivers.EUR: CPI Flash Estimate beat at 3.8% vs 3.7%, but FX response was muted at -0.036%.
currency_drivers.JPY: Tokyo Core CPI beat at 2.7% vs 2.4%, giving JPY a normal 0.067% lift.
currency_drivers.GBP: No own release; closed at its best, driven by broad dollar weakness.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own release; strongest major, benefiting from high-beta demand and USD weakness.
currency_drivers.CAD: No own release; early +0.12% attempt fully rejected, ending weakest at -0.277%.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own release; led +0.44% early then gave back 70%.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own release; sold to -0.13%, recovered 60%.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD had four legs: +48.3 pips on open, -40.7 pips into Europe, +57.6 pips on NFP, then -26.3 pips late; only the NFP leg had a catalyst.

polarity_reads.read: Normal USD-negative reaction (0.097% own impulse; Gold +0.866%, USD/JPY -0.292%) implies dollar longs were vulnerable to a payroll miss.
Normal JPY-positive 0.067% lift despite modest size suggests BoJ tightening expectations were already well priced.
Muted EUR response (-0.036% inside noise floor) despite upside surprise indicates the upside inflation scenario was already discounted.

scenarios.name: Rangebound digestion
scenarios.thesis: The dollar consolidates after the NFP shock; EUR/USD and other majors remain within their day ranges as markets await ISM services.
triggers: ISM Services PMI prints near 55.1 forecast
No new tariff or oil headlines
scenarios.invalidation: A sustained break of EUR/USD’s 70-pip range would signal directional continuation.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD jumped 57.6 pips on NFP then faded 26.3 pips; with no fresh catalyst it should stay within its 70-pip day range.

scenarios.name: Risk-on extension
scenarios.thesis: High-beta currencies extend as the payroll miss feeds faster Fed easing expectations and commodity/equities stay bid.
scenarios.invalidation: A drop in AUD/USD back below the day's midpoint would negate risk-on continuation.

pair_paths.rationale: AUD was strongest major (+0.331%) and most sensitive to NFP; follow-through can test the upper bound of its 65.5-pip range.
USD/JPY fell 72.5 pips in the Asian leg and remains heavy after NFP; risk-on weakens USD/JPY as USD loses ground.

scenarios.name: USD bounce
scenarios.thesis: The dollar partially retraces as NFP overshoot fades or risk sentiment turns on oil/geopolitics, lifting USD/CHF and USD/JPY.
scenarios.invalidation: A move below DXY 101.675 or a fresh USD/CHF low would invalidate the bounce.

pair_paths.rationale: USD/CHF fell 60.2 pips in its main down leg, then bounced 32.5 pips; a USD recovery can retrace toward the upper end of its 101.6-pip range.
USD/JPY closed near 157.857 after a 68.8-pip late bounce; a dollar rebound could push it back toward the upper part of its 130.2-pip range.

risks.risk: ISM Services PMI surprises to the upside
risks.why_it_matters: Would challenge the NFP-driven Fed easing trade and support a dollar rebound.
Threats of resumed Iran bombing can trigger risk-off into CHF and JPY, reversing high-beta gains.

risks.risk: Fed speakers push back on NFP implications
risks.why_it_matters: Hawkish comments could reprice rate expectations and unwind dollar losses.
risks.watch: Any Fed speakers after the employment report

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: OPEC-JMMC meetings at 11:15 and US ISM Services PMI at 16:00 are the next scheduled catalysts; ISM services is the main event that can confirm or fade the NFP-driven dollar move.
